ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Four vials were set up to investigate bacterial transformation. Vials 1 and 2 each contained E. coli bacteria that had been made competent and had then been mixed with a plasmid containing the gene for ampicillin (pAMP) resistance. Vials 3 and 4 both contained E. coli that had also been made competent but had not been mixed with a plasmid. Each vial of bacteria was poured onto a nutrient agar plate. Vials 1 and 3 were poured onto plates that contained the antibiotic ampicillin. Vials 2 and 4 were poured onto plates that did not contain ampicillin.

This figure shows what the nutrient agar plates looked like. The shaded plates represent extensive growth, and the dots represent individual bacterial colonies.

Which of the following statements explains why there was no growth on Plate 3?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are 4 Petri dishes in the image, labeled respectively From test tube 1 to From test tube 4. There are multiple black dots in Plate 1, indicating that bacterial colonies have grown; Plate 2 and Plate 4 appear to have uniform light gray areas; inside Plate 3 there are no visible colonies or traces of growth. Reasoning: The question background states that bacteria from test tube/vial 3 were inoculated onto agar medium containing ampicillin. Medium containing ampicillin will inhibit the growth of bacteria without a resistance gene, and only bacteria that have been successfully transformed and carry the ampicillin-resistance gene can grow. Because Plate 3 has no growth under ampicillin selection conditions, these bacteria were not transformed.
